trails.title: Revisions
trails.subtitle: three revisions that read the stack
trails.say: The fourth stage: the combiner anchors on the camera member, or the screenshot member when the gate fired, silences the generated-side evidence under a present capture and otherwise pools it; the frame seam reruns the pipeline on a dark frame's interior; the preview tail flips a small image to real only when two reads agree. The Result stage writes what they leave.

steps.title: The combiner: the anchor and the pool

entries.note: Takes the anchor's P(AI) and operating point; a present capture leaves the anchor standing, otherwise the combiner pools it with the evidence members its file names.

entries.anchor: if a < anchor.gateCeiling { z -= rescue.w * max(0, -maxLogit) }
entries.note: Adds each evidence member's generated push to the capped anchor logit, and subtracts the consensus rescue only while the anchor sits under the gate ceiling. On 97,181 capture-absent store rows, taking the human push out moved 68 calls.
Caps each evidence member's logit at 2. The reference combiner also let an art-pair head lower the art logit; taking it out moved 29 of 97,181 store calls, 19 of them to the right label.

An evidence member's influence, recorded in the combiner's record: its generated push, or, while every member reads real under the gate, the shared rescue. Without the rescue a real wildlife photograph flipped to generated on 2026-10-19.

trails.title: Watermark signing
trails.subtitle: an image to its signature, nothing added to it
trails.say: From an image to its watermark, with nothing added to its pixels: the native plane is cut into 32-pixel tiles, the warp residual gives each tile a fragility rate, each tile becomes four ordinal bits against its neighbours, sixteen tiles pack into a 64-bit word, and the words are named by their SHA-256.

steps.title: The command reads the image at its own size

entries.note: veilgarde watermark sign prints the signature as one line of vw1 text, or as JSON with --json, and names its grid, its bits and its id on stderr. Nothing is written into the image.
Signs an image with nothing added to its pixels: its tile codes at native resolution, read from the grid anchored at the top-left corner.

entries.anchor: let pixels = try ImageLoading.rgbPixels(cg, width: cg.width, height: cg.height)
entries.note: Reads the RGB plane once at its native size, with no cap and no padding. A crop must land on the same pixels in the same tiles as its source, and a resize would move every one.

steps.title: Every tile's fragility, by the warp residual

entries.anchor: let fr = WarpResidual.fragility(low: low, high: high)
entries.note: Measures every full tile's fragility rate from a given origin: each batch of tiles warped at both strengths, the residual read, the rate taken.
The forward and inverse tap tables for both strengths, built once per process: they are constants.
Builds the table pair for the weaker strength and the stronger one.
Moves a tile's four corners by the fixed displacements times the strength, and keeps the reference's inverse of the inverse for the way back, cast once from float64.
The 16 homographies as corner moves in [−1, 1], a literal table: every signature ever written was read through these warps.
The round trip through the 16 homographies and back, the error averaged over channels and trials, then a 9×9 Gaussian high-pass at σ 1.5.
A tile's fragility rate: how much more of it the stronger warp loses than the weaker, per unit of strength.

entries.anchor: if v > g[nr, nc] { bits[r * g.cols + c] |= 1 << k }
entries.note: Turns each tile's fragility into four ordinal bits against its east, south, south-east and north-east neighbours, masking every comparison that leaves the image. An ordinal bit survives any monotone change of the residual's gain.
entries.cite: test:tile codes: four ordinal bits against E, S, SE, NE, masked at the edges

entries.note: A signature holds its version, 32-pixel tiles, 4-tile sections, the tile grid's rows and columns, and the packed words.
Four by four tiles, 128 pixels, pack into one 64-bit word in row-major order, with a mask word beside it. No hash folds them, so a bit that differs is one bit of distance, not a different word.
The one line sign prints: vw1: and the binary in base64url.

entries.anchor: for w in codes { withUnsafeBytes(of: w.littleEndian) { d.append(contentsOf: $0) } }
entries.note: The binary: a magic, the version, the tile and section sizes, the grid's rows and columns, the section count, then every code word and every mask word, little-endian.
The id is the SHA-256 of exactly those bytes, so two signatures of the same pixels are the same id.

trails.title: Watermark matching
trails.subtitle: a crop or a re-encode to its place and score
trails.say: From an image and a signature to a match: the signature is read back and checked, the image's codes are read at sixteen grid phases, each phase slides over the signature at every whole-tile offset, the best agreement is the match, and the acceptance and the invariance run hold the signatures to their record.

steps.title: The command reads the image and the signature

entries.note: The JSON form: the words as 16-digit hex, since a 64-bit number is not safe in every JSON reader, and a stated id that must be the words' own, so an edited signature is refused.

steps.title: The image is read at sixteen grid phases

entries.anchor: public init(phases: [Int] = [0, 8, 16, 24], minimumBits: Int = 256, threshold: Double = 0.75, margin: Int = 1) {
entries.note: The defaults: a phase every 8 pixels, a match at 0.75 over at least 256 compared bits, and offsets that run one tile past every edge.

entries.anchor: out.append((px, py, TileCodeGrid(plane.fragility(originX: px, originY: py))))
entries.note: A crop starts at an arbitrary pixel, so its tiles straddle the signature's. Its codes are read from 16 origins, every 8 pixels in each direction, which puts one within 4 pixels of the signed grid.

entries.anchor: let region = array[originY..<(originY + rows * ts), originX..<(originX + cols * ts), 0...]
entries.note: The same measurement as signing, from a shifted origin: only the tiles that fit whole past it.

steps.title: Each phase slides over the signature

entries.anchor: guard let b = Matcher.best(crop: crop, stored: stored, margin: options.margin, minimumBits: options.minimumBits) else { continue }
entries.note: For each phase, asks the matcher for its best whole-tile offset, and keeps the best score over every phase, more compared bits breaking a tie.

entries.anchor: public var tileCodes: TileCodeGrid { Sectioning.unpack(codes: codes, masks: masks, rows: rows, cols: cols) }
entries.note: Unpacks the section words back into the tile grid, so the matcher compares tile against tile.
Slides the crop's codes over the signature's at every whole-tile offset and counts the disagreeing bits among those both sides measured; the offset with the best score wins.

steps.title: The best agreement is the match

entries.note: How far the score sits above chance, in coin-flip units for the bits compared. It does not replace the 0.75 floor: every crop that compared 256 bits scored at least 9.2 above chance, but strangers reached 11.9, since the matcher keeps the best of thousands of placements.

entries.anchor: public var pixelX: Int { offsetX * WarpConstants.tileSize - phaseX }
entries.note: Where the image's top-left corner sits on the signed image: the offset in tiles times 32, less the phase.
veilgarde watermark verify gives the same verdict as an exit code: 0 for a match, 1 for none.

steps.title: The acceptance and the invariance hold v1 to its record

entries.anchor: let report = try WatermarkAcceptance.run(sample.map { ($0.url, $0.label) }, settings: settings, note: note,
entries.note: veilgarde watermark accept samples final_mixed by a seed, half real and half generated, and writes each image's row as it is measured, so a long run that stops keeps what it measured.
Draws the same images from the same seed as the 2026-10-19 run did, each label shuffled by its own seeded generator.

entries.anchor: let cross = Watermark.match(codes: cropCodes, against: other, options: options)
entries.note: Signs every image, then measures each: a self-match, a crop of half its area at a random pixel offset, a JPEG at quality 0.75, the crop against the next image's signature, and on every fourth image the crop resized.
The share of ones at each bit position. On 198 images every position sat between 0.496 and 0.498, so no bit is close to a constant.

The kill criterion, fixed in code before the run: the crop must match with its offset in 60% of images, the median JPEG score must reach 0.75, and some threshold must reach 80% crop recall with at most 5% false matches. On 198 images v1 passed with 73.2%, 0.958, and 81.3% recall at 0.73 with no false match, on 2026-10-19 and again on 2026-10-21 after the residual moved.
Signs the battery's 105 images again and lists every way a signature departs from the recorded one. After the detection change and after the residual moved, all 105 were equal.

trails.title: Audio to the residual
trails.subtitle: a clip to the picture the warp round trip reads, and its signature
trails.say: From a clip to its watermark, with nothing written into the sound: the clip is read through one door, mixed to one channel at the profile's rate, cut into windowed frames and transformed on the GPU, each bin's magnitude mapped to one of 256 grey levels in a picture the lens reads unchanged, and that picture signed by the watermark's own residual: the same sixteen warps, the same fragility rate, the same four bits a tile.

steps.title: The command reads the clip through one door

entries.anchor: let image = try AudioWatermark.picture(clip, profile: try profile.resolve())
entries.note: veilgarde audio sign draws the clip's picture under the chosen profile and prints the picture's signature as vw1 text or JSON, naming its grid, its bits and its fragility on stderr. Nothing is written into the sound.
Every audio command reads its clip through the carrier's one door.

entries.anchor: for c in 0..<channelCount { channels[c].append(contentsOf: UnsafeBufferPointer(start: data[c], count: n)) }
entries.note: Door one decodes whatever CoreAudio reads as Float32 at the file's own rate and channel count, chunk by chunk to the end. It is one of the two files that import AVFoundation, so a change to how sound is read is one file.

steps.title: One channel at the profile's rate

entries.note: A clip's picture is three steps: the analysis signal, its transform, and the transform drawn as grey levels.

entries.anchor: let resampled = try AudioConverting.resampled(clip.mono, from: clip.sampleRate, to: profile.sampleRate)
entries.note: The channels are averaged and resampled to the profile's rate. A clip already at that rate keeps its samples exactly, so a cut of it holds its source's samples.
Door two resamples with AVAudioConverter at its mastering algorithm and highest quality, fed once and flushed, and trims the output to the length the two rates imply.

entries.anchor: public static let music = SpectrogramProfile(name: "music", sampleRate: 44_100, fftSize: 2048, hop: 512
entries.note: The two profiles the owner fixed: music at 44.1 kHz with 2048-sample frames every 512, a picture 1024 rows tall, and speech at 16 kHz with 1024 every 256, 512 rows tall. They are to merge once the research says how.

steps.title: Frames under a window, transformed on the GPU

entries.note: The frames go to Frigate's FFT in chunks, and the real and imaginary parts come back as Float; everything else runs on the CPU in Double. The chunk size changes no value.

entries.anchor: for n in n0..<n1 { out[base + n] = Float(x[start + n] * w[n]) }
entries.note: Half a frame of zeros on each side, then a frame every hop, each multiplied by the window. Zeros rather than a reflection, so a frame depends only on the samples inside it and a cut's inner frames equal its source's.
A periodic Hann built in Double: its four overlapping copies square-sum to 1.5 at every inner sample, which is what makes the inverse exact.
entries.cite: test:the periodic Hann: w[0] = 0, w[N/2] = 1, Σw = N/2, Σw² = 3N/8, and four copies sum to 1.5

steps.title: A magnitude to a grey level

entries.anchor: g[(height - bin) * width + t] = GrayMapping.level(magnitude: m, profile: profile)
entries.note: The picture keeps bins 1 to N/2, the highest in the top row and time left to right, one byte a bin. The DC bin is left out, so an offset in the sound cannot reach the picture.
A magnitude becomes one of 256 levels on a fixed scale from −96 to 0 dBFS, 0.376 dB a level. A fixed scale, never the clip's own peak, so a cut's pixels equal its source's.
0 dBFS is a full-scale sine's peak bin under the periodic Hann, a quarter of the frame length.

steps.title: A picture the lens reads unchanged

entries.note: A clip's signature is the image watermark's signature of its picture, with nothing bypassed.

entries.anchor: space: CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB(), bitmapInfo: CGImageAlphaInfo.noneSkipLast.rawValue) else { return nil }
entries.note: The bitmap is 8-bit device RGB with no alpha and the level in all three channels, the context the lens draws into, so the lens reads these bytes as they are; the study's figures are written through the same function.
entries.cite: test:flat device RGB, R = G = B, the lens reads the bytes unchanged, and the levels read back

steps.title: The same round trip, on sound

entries.note: From here the code is the image watermark's own, unchanged: a picture of sound is a plane like any photograph's.
The picture's bytes become a plane at native size, 1024 or 512 pixels tall and as wide as the clip has frames.

entries.anchor: let tiles = region.reshaped([rows, ts, cols, ts, 3]).transposed(0, 2, 1, 3, 4).reshaped([rows * cols, ts * ts, 3])
entries.note: Every full 32 by 32 tile is cut out. On sound a tile is 32 frames by 32 bins: 371 ms by 689 Hz under the music profile, 512 ms by 500 Hz under speech.

entries.anchor: return R - batchedGaussianBlur(R, kernelSize: WarpConstants.highPassKernel, sigma: WarpConstants.highPassSigma)
entries.note: Each tile goes through the sixteen homographies and back at two strengths, and the high frequencies of what the round trip loses are kept. On a picture of sound that loss is read off the texture harmonics, onsets and noise draw.

steps.title: Four bits a tile, and the words

entries.note: Each tile's fragility against its east, south, south-east and north-east neighbours gives four ordinal bits. On sound east is later in time and south is lower in pitch.
The signature is a vw1 signature like an image's; its tile rows, 32 or 16, name the profile it was drawn under.

trails.title: Audio matching
trails.subtitle: a cut found in time, and the picture back to sound
trails.say: From a clip and a signature to a match, and from the picture back to sound: the signature names its profile by its tile rows, the clip's picture is read at four grid phases along time, each slides over the signature, the best column becomes seconds, the transform goes back to sound through the window-square sum, and the acceptance holds it all to the image lane's kill criterion.

steps.title: The command reads the cut and the signature

entries.anchor: let r = try AudioWatermark.match(try loadClip(audio), against: try WatermarkCommand.signature(signature),
entries.note: veilgarde audio match prints where a clip sits on a signature, in tiles and in seconds, with its score and its z-score.
The signature is read as the image watermark reads one: vw1 text, or a file holding vw1 text or JSON.

steps.title: The profile from the signature's rows

entries.anchor: let p = try profile ?? self.profile(of: signature)
entries.note: Unless the caller names a profile, the signature's own is used, so a music signature is never read as speech.

entries.anchor: guard let p = SpectrogramProfile.inferred(rows: signature.rows) else {
entries.note: A signature whose tile rows fit no profile is refused.
32 tile rows is music and 16 is speech.

entries.anchor: let result = Watermark.match(codes: try phaseCodes(image, phases: options.phases), against: signature, options: options)
entries.note: The clip's picture is matched with the watermark's own matcher and thresholds, a score of 0.75 over at least 256 bits.

entries.anchor: return phases.map { px in (px, 0, TileCodeGrid(plane.fragility(originX: px, originY: 0))) }
entries.note: The grid is read at 0, 8, 16 and 24 frames along time and at row 0 alone: a cut keeps every frequency, so four reads replace the image's sixteen.
Each phase slides over the signature at every whole-tile offset, and the best agreement wins.
The score is the share of the bits both sides measured that agree.
The matched column times the hop over the rate is where the cut starts in the signed clip.
The matcher may still slide a row up or down. A true match of a cut has none, and the acceptance counts the matches that do.
veilgarde audio roundtrip rebuilds the sound two ways, from the exact transform and from the 8-bit picture, and reports how far it moved.
The picture's levels replace the magnitudes under the original phase, and the transform goes back to sound.

entries.anchor: let scale = GrayMapping.magnitude(level: level, profile: profile) / m
entries.note: Each complex value is scaled to the centre of its level's step, and level 0 is silence.
The windowed overlap-add is divided by the window-square sum at every sample, so the exact transform returns the sound to float precision.

entries.anchor: let snr: Double = noise == 0 ? .infinity : (signal == 0 ? -.infinity : 10 * log10(signal / noise))
entries.note: The signal-to-noise ratio, the largest sample error and the log-spectral deviation say how far the sound moved.

entries.anchor: let report = try AudioAcceptance.run(inputs, settings: settings, note: note, measured: { try? rows?.append($0) })
entries.note: veilgarde audio accept samples clips, runs the acceptance and prints whether v1 on sound is killed.

entries.anchor: let m = Watermark.match(codes: codes, against: signature, options: options)
entries.note: Each clip is matched against itself, by a half-length cut at a random sample, with its first fractions of a hop dropped too when asked and the best kept, by an AAC re-encode and by the next clip's cut, as the image acceptance does with crops, JPEG and strangers.

entries.anchor: let used = offered.isEmpty ? requested : (offered.filter { $0 <= requested }.max() ?? offered.min() ?? requested)
entries.note: The re-encode is AAC at the profile's rate, 128 kb/s for music and 64 for speech, or the highest rate the encoder offers below it, and both are recorded.

entries.anchor: let correlation = MLXFFT.irfft(spectrumB * spectrumA.conjugate(), n: size)
entries.note: The decode's lag is measured by cross-correlation and corrected before the match.

The kill criterion is the image lane's, fixed before the run: a cut found with its offset in at least 60% of clips, a median re-encode score of at least 0.75, and 80% recall at no more than 5% false matches.
entries.cite: test:each rule kills on its own, and the image lane's summarize agrees on the same rows

trails.title: Audio time phases
trails.subtitle: a clip's fragility dense in time, its recurrences and its time steps
trails.say: The time-phase study, the owner's slicing idea as an instrument: a clip's picture is read by the watermark's own residual at every time phase, so the fragility becomes a trace dense in time, with the residual's slope finer than a tile beside it; sections of half a second to two seconds are compared with the whole trace at every offset; the trace's spectrum gives the time steps that stand above their baseline and carry harmonics; and the rows fixed before the run read the result.

steps.title: The command and the clip's report

entries.anchor: let (report, trace) = try TimePhaseStudy.measure(input.clip, path: input.name, kind: input.kind, profile: p, sectionSeconds: lengths, subHop: subHop, reencode: aac)
entries.note: veilgarde audio phases studies clips from files, cut into segments, or synthetic clips with a known answer, and writes one report and one figure per clip and a summary for the run.

entries.anchor: let trace = try FragilityTrace.measure(clip, profile: profile, subHop: subHop)
entries.note: One clip's report: the trace, the sections' recurrences, the periodicity of T and of E, the flags the hypothesis rows read, and the AAC re-encode's trace beside the original when asked.

entries.anchor: let signal = try AnalysisSignal(clip, profile: profile)
entries.note: A clip's trace at frame resolution, or at quarter or eighth hops.

entries.anchor: let shifted = AnalysisSignal(profile: signal.profile, samples: Array(signal.samples.dropFirst(delta)))
entries.note: For a finer time axis the signal is shifted by a fraction of a hop and analysed again; the framing centres frame t on sample t times the hop of whatever it is given, so no framing code changes.

The watermark's grid read at all 32 time phases and interleaved: T at frame f is the fragility of the tile anchored there, and at every tile boundary it is the signature's own value. From the same pass, E: the residual's slope per picture column, averaged over the tiles that cover it.
entries.cite: test:T at the tile boundaries is the signature's own grid, exactly, and E averages to T

entries.anchor: let diff = MLX.abs(tiles.reshaped([N, 1, ts * ts, 3]) - returned.reshaped([N, WarpConstants.trials, ts * ts, 3]))
entries.note: The round trip's error per pixel, before it is averaged over the trials and high-passed: what E reads column by column.

entries.anchor: fr[(r * tc + f) * subHop + q] = t.fr[r * t.columns + f]
entries.note: The shifted traces interleaved as column subHop times f plus q, so each column stands for one fraction of a hop.
The owner's slicing: sections of 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 s, each compared with the whole trace at frame resolution.

entries.anchor: f[r * tc + c] = fr[r * columns + c * subHop]
entries.note: A finer trace read back at frame resolution for the sections, every subHop-th column.

entries.anchor: for o in 0...(columns - l) where abs(o - a) >= l + ts {
entries.note: A section's block slid over the whole trace: the Pearson correlation and the matcher's bit agreement at every offset, offsets that share a picture column with the section left out, a peak at z of 4 against the admitted offsets' median and MAD.

entries.anchor: let residue = ((o - a) % step + step) % step
entries.note: Three or more peaks congruent modulo one spacing are a recurrence: the spacing is the step, the section's start modulo it the phase. On music that is a returning phrase, and the report says recurrence, never generated.
entries.cite: test:a block planted three times is a recurrence with its step and phase

steps.title: The time steps, from the spectrum

entries.anchor: let e = PeriodicityScan.scan((0..<trace.rows).map(trace.residualRow), lagMin: 2, columnSeconds: trace.columnSeconds, columnSamples: trace.columnSamples, probes: probes)
entries.note: T is scanned for periods of 32 frames and longer, E from two steps up: E is the instrument for anything under a tile.

The rows windowed, zero-padded and transformed on Frigate's FFT, their power pooled and read in the log over a running-median baseline; a line is a local maximum at z of 4, confirmed by its harmonics at z of 2, and a fundamental when no lower confirmed line divides it.
entries.cite: test:a planted pulse train of period 21 is a confirmed fundamental; a bare sinusoid is a line without harmonics

entries.note: Each row standardized and freed of its centred four-second moving average, so the slow drift does not swamp the lines.

A corpus summary: the confirmed fundamentals of every clip, the dominant steps binned in milliseconds, the clips flagged under 20 ms, and the codec frame found in re-encodes. The hypothesis rows are judged on these counts.
A figure per clip: T with each tile row eight pixels tall, E beneath it, and the two spectra's z over the band as strips.
